causes.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, retailers faced increased labor and sanitation costs. Many companies boosted wages and invested in safety measures to protect workers. The environment accelerated e-commerce adoption and changed shopping behavior; even as online demand surged, operating expenses remained elevated.

source_info.title: Pandemic drives up labor and sanitation costs for retailers

effects.text: On March 4, 2021, Costco reported quarterly results showing net income of $951 million on revenue of $44.77 billion, but its profit missed analysts' estimates as pandemic-related charges and higher labor costs weighed on margins. The company noted that overall online sales jumped 75.8 % year-over-year.

source_info.title: Pandemic shoots up costs for Costco, profit misses estimates

causal_reasoning_chain.description: The COVID-19 pandemic forced retailers to implement extensive health and safety measures. Companies raised wages to retain essential workers and spent heavily on sanitizing stores. Online shopping surged, requiring additional investments in supply chains.
These costs increased operating expenses across the retail sector. Even as e-commerce sales grew, profit margins came under pressure.

When Costco reported its fiscal Q2 2021 results on 2021-03-04, it recorded net income of $951 million but missed profit expectations; shares dipped about 1.6 % in after-hours trading (share price change −1.6 %).

rationale: Pandemic-induced safety and labor costs weighed on Costco's profit even though online sales surged.
counterfactual_analysis: If the pandemic had not forced retailers to raise wages and spend on sanitization, Costco might have met or exceeded profit expectations.

adversarial_confounders.text: Gasoline price volatility and foreign exchange could also affect earnings performance.
adversarial_confounders.impact: External cost factors may partially explain the profit miss and stock reaction.

details.pestel_factor: Social - Health crisis and elevated safety expectations for retail workers and shoppers
details.commentary: COVID-19 raised expectations for protective equipment, cleaning, and crowd management inside stores. Meeting these social and health expectations forced Costco to spend more on labor and safety measures, weighing on margins despite strong traffic.

The pandemic drove up costs in the short term, but investments in safety and staffing helped maintain trust and membership loyalty. As conditions normalized and one-off expenses faded, that loyalty supported ongoing sales, gradually balancing the earlier profit squeeze.
